title: India's August Exports Surge 25.4% as Trade Deficit Narrows Sharply
excerpt: Exports hit $82.68 billion in August while a 57% plunge in gold imports helped push the overall deficit down to $9.41 billion.
body:
• India's overall exports — merchandise plus services — rose 25.4% year-on-year to $82.68 billion in August 2026, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Tuesday, as export growth outpaced imports for the month.
  • The overall trade deficit narrowed to $9.41 billion from $11.62 billion a year earlier; the merchandise deficit shrank to $26.86 billion, well below the $32 billion economists had expected.
  • A sharp 57% plunge in gold imports — down to $2.3 billion from $5.4 billion — provided major relief to the trade account, aided by Prime Minister Modi's call to curb gold purchases.
  • The rupee still fell to a more-than-one-month low against the dollar as surging oil prices and bets on a US Federal Reserve rate hike this week weighed on sentiment.

India's export engine accelerated in August, with overall exports climbing 25.4% from a year earlier and the country's trade deficit narrowing sharply — a rare bright spot on a day when the rupee tumbled to its weakest level in more than a month.

Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal told reporters on Tuesday that overall exports, covering merchandise and services, reached an estimated $82.68 billion in August 2026, up from $65.93 billion in August 2025. The overall trade deficit narrowed to $9.41 billion from $11.62 billion a year earlier.

"The export growth momentum accelerated further in August," Agrawal said, pointing to strengthening demand and diversification across commodities and global markets.

The numbers behind the headline

Merchandise exports rose 26.12% in dollar terms to $43.81 billion, from $34.74 billion a year earlier, while imports grew at a slower pace to $70.67 billion. The merchandise trade deficit consequently shrank to $26.86 billion from $27.20 billion — a figure that came in well below the $32 billion economists had pencilled in, according to a Reuters poll, and a marked improvement on the roughly $32 billion gap recorded in July.

Services trade stayed strong as well: services exports are estimated at $38.87 billion, up 24.61% from $31.19 billion a year earlier, with services imports rising to $21.42 billion.

Gold's 57% slump

One of the biggest contributors to the narrower deficit was a dramatic fall in gold imports, which dropped 57% to $2.3 billion in August from $5.4 billion in the same month last year — meaning India bought roughly $3.1 billion less gold.

The slump follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal earlier this year urging Indians to refrain from buying gold for a year to protect foreign exchange reserves, made as the West Asia crisis pushed oil prices higher and pressured the rupee. India's gold import bill had hit an all-time high of $71.98 billion in 2025-26 even as physical volumes fell, reflecting elevated global prices.

"The export growth momentum accelerated further in August."

— Rajesh Agrawal, Commerce Secretary

Diversification story

India is seeking to diversify its export markets. Its trade deal with Britain is now in force, and a broader pact with the European Union is moving toward implementation — steps that could open greater access for Indian goods. Agrawal credited export growth to engineering goods, petroleum products, chemicals and textiles, with the major demand coming from the US, EU and BRICS economies.

The resilience also showed up in the current account: India's current account deficit stood at $4.2 billion, or 0.5% of GDP, in the April-June quarter (Q1 FY2027), according to Reserve Bank of India data released earlier this month — broadly steady despite rising global prices for oil, LPG and fertilisers linked to the West Asia crisis.

Currency and market pressure

The trade data landed on a turbulent day for Indian markets. The rupee fell to its weakest level in more than a month on Tuesday but held above 96 per dollar — settling at 95.9550 — as likely central bank intervention limited losses driven by surging oil prices and bets on a US rate hike this week. Brent crude rose more than 2% to $108.20 a barrel.

Broadening inflation has prompted traders to add to wagers on a Reserve Bank of India rate hike next month, with both Citi and Deutsche Bank bringing forward their rate-hike calls from December to October, according to Reuters. The benchmark 10-year bond yield climbed to its highest since mid-May, and the Nifty 50 ended lower by about 1%.

What to watch

The key question is whether August's export acceleration holds. Economists note the narrower deficit owed much to the gold import collapse — a volatile line item — while the energy import bill continues to widen with crude above $108. With the Fed's policy decision due Wednesday and the Bank of Japan meeting Friday, India's exporters will be watching global rate signals as closely as their order books.
image_caption: A container ship at an Indian port. India’s merchandise exports rose 25.4% in August while the trade deficit narrowed sharply to $26.86 billion.
nri_angle: Strong export data supports the India growth story that diaspora investors track in portfolios and remittance decisions; the gold import collapse also hints at changing festive-season buying behaviour among Indian households.
author: Diaspora Desk
